items.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020
items.q: Billy did stuff for Nelson Riddle and all these people you know.

ctx.x: Were the writers and arrangers always at the sessions? © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

Kind of yes more so than not. Sometimes, like for instance I did the “Tony Randall Show” and the main writer was Pat Williams. But Pat wrote the theme song and then he would farm out to ghost writing with Sammy Nestico. And Sammy Nestico was the writer, the ghost writer for everybody out there. He and Billy Byers. Billy Byers was one of the most insane, greatest skilled writers I think I’ve ever seen in my life. Billy could sit and write a chart without a score, put it in his head, and he’d come back in 45…
Yeah right. I imagine you did your share of rock & roll dates?
